title: Earth's Four Systems
seo_title: Grade 5 Earth's Systems Worksheets: Geosphere, Hydrosphere, Atmosphere and Biosphere
standard_text: Develop a model using an example to describe ways the geosphere, biosphere, hydrosphere, and/or atmosphere interact.
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 science worksheets on Earth's systems (NGSS 5-ESS2-1): the geosphere, hydrosphere, atmosphere and biosphere and how they interact, with real examples like waves, wind, plants and volcanoes. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Earth's four systems are always changing each other.
key_sub: Geosphere = rock and soil, hydrosphere = water and ice, atmosphere = air, biosphere = living things. Waves, wind, plants and volcanoes link them.
body_html:
How to think about it

Scientists think of Earth as four connected systems:

SystemWhat it includes
geosphererock, soil, sand, mountains
hydrosphereoceans, rivers, lakes, ice, groundwater
atmosphereair: nitrogen, oxygen, carbon dioxide
biosphereall living things, including people

The systems are always interacting. Ocean waves (hydrosphere) wear away rock (geosphere). Wind (atmosphere) piles up sand dunes. Plants (biosphere) take carbon dioxide from the air and their roots break rocks. A volcano sends ash into the air.

Example

A river carves a canyon. Which systems interact?

River water: hydrosphere.

Rock of the canyon: geosphere.

Answer: hydrosphere and geosphere

Example

Plants take in carbon dioxide. Which systems interact?

Plants: biosphere.

Carbon dioxide in the air: atmosphere.

Answer: biosphere and atmosphere

Common mistakes

  • Putting rain or ice only in the atmosphere. All water and ice belong to the hydrosphere.
  • Leaving people out of the biosphere.
  • Thinking the systems work separately. A change in one affects the others.

faq.a: The geosphere (rock and soil), hydrosphere (all water and ice), atmosphere (air) and biosphere (all living things, including people).

faq.q: What is an example of the hydrosphere and geosphere interacting?
faq.a: Ocean waves wear away rocks along a beach, or a river carves a canyon.

faq.q: How does the biosphere affect the atmosphere?
faq.a: Plants take in carbon dioxide and give off oxygen and water vapor, and animals breathe in oxygen.

faq.q: Are clouds part of the atmosphere or the hydrosphere?
faq.a: Clouds are made of water drops or ice, so the water in them is part of the hydrosphere, even though it floats in the atmosphere.
